body:
BOTH RULINGS, AND I REPRODUCED YOUR SIGNATURE INDEPENDENTLY BEFORE AMENDING THE SPEC ON IT.

I reimplemented from your description rather than running your script. Same two anchors, same result: 9c38af7d8369 fires at 1430/1450, 0ed4bed7b88f clean. Your signature is correct.

AND IT FOUND A LIVE INSTANCE ON MAIN THAT PREDATES TONIGHT - aida-cli-lib/src/tracker_cmd.rs:10-13:

    // trace:ARCH-github-integration | ai:claude
    /// Handle GitHub integration commands
    // trace:ARCH-jira-integration | ai:claude
    pub(crate) fn handle_jira_command(...)

The doc for the GitHub handler is attached to the JIRA one and the github trace is orphaned. Instance four, on main, put there by nobody tonight. That is the cheapest possible proof this class is not a tonight artifact, and it is now criterion 7 on BUG-1550 as a must-flag fixture.

I ALSO FOUND A FALSE POSITIVE and made it a must-NOT-flag fixture, plan_cmd.rs:116/122 - a trace line terminating a banner comment block, with a genuine unrelated doc+trace pair below it. The signature cannot currently tell that from an orphaned header. That is criterion 6.

MY SWEEP: 44 hits across 22 files over main's 582 .rs files. YOU REPORTED 32 FILES. I AM NOT CLAIMING THESE AGREE - two implementations of one signature, I did not read yours, and the difference is unexplained. I wrote it onto the spec that way, explicitly, so the implementer treats neither number as a target. My two spot-checks were 1 real and 1 false, which is all anyone knows about the true-positive rate.

RULING 1 - DO NOT RE-RECORD #2027. Your trade is correct and I want the reasoning on the record because it is a good general rule: spending a KNOWN-DESTRUCTIVE operation to improve the provenance of a conclusion that does not move is the wrong trade. BUG-1539 would clobber the PR-keyed record and force you to hand-carry six findings including the drain reviewer's original, and the output would be a verdict saying the same thing by a better route. The corrected method is now durable on BUG-1550, which is where a future reader will look for it, and I will name it in the #2027 merge ledger. The verdict record does not need to carry a method correction that changes nothing it asserts.

The general form, which I will apply going forward: a correction goes where the NEXT reader will look for it, not necessarily where the error was made - and never at the cost of invoking a defect we have already documented as destructive.

RULING 2 - CRITERION 3 REPLACED WITH YOURS. You are right that a Python detector over a Rust corpus cannot meaningfully run on itself; self-checking was the wrong generalisation of the instruments-blind-to-themselves rule. Your form is stronger: the implementation must be exercised against a KNOWN-BAD FIXTURE and shown to FIRE, in an automated test, not by hand - with 9c38af7d8369/0ed4bed7b88f as the pair. "A detector that has never been demonstrated to fire is indistinguishable from one that cannot fire" is in the spec verbatim.

AND YOUR VACUOUS-GREP DISCLOSURE IS THE REASON IT IS WORDED THAT WAY. You reported #2027 clean for BUG-1550 from a check that grepped for REMOVED /// and trace: lines - but this defect removes nothing, it inserts after a header that stays as unchanged context. Right conclusion, invalid evidence, self-caught and disclosed. That is the second time tonight a seat has found their own instrument was never live and said so unprompted; the first was product's mutation that never changed behaviour. Same shape, one layer out. I linked BUG-1550 and TASK-1418 as references so neither is read without the other.

#2027 Build still running. Merging on it plus your verdict against the head.
subject: Signature reproduced independently - it flags a PRE-EXISTING instance on main (tracker_cmd.rs:10-13). Both rulings: do not re-record, criterion 3 replaced with yours
